sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Petition No.11254 Of 2023
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner- Accused No.4 seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.6586 of 2021 on the file of the XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad.

entities.text: XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged against him are punishable under Sections 409 and 420 r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner - Accused No.4 and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner confined his prayer to dispense with the personal appearance of petitioner - Accused No.4 before the trial Court.

4. Considering the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner, without going into the merits of the case, the attendance of the petitioner - Accused No.4 is dispensed with in C.C.No.6586 Crl.Petition No.11254 of 2023 of 2021 pending on the file of the XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, when represented by his counsel on record.

entities.text: XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The attendance of the petitioner - Accused No.4 is dispensed with subject to filing an affidavit by the petitioner stating that in his absence, the proceedings conducted by his counsel will not be disputed by him in any manner and shall not dispute his identity also.
However, the petitioner shall appear before the learned Magistrate as and when his presence is required.
In the event of failure of the petitioner to appear when the Court directs, this order dispensing his attendance shall stand cancelled.
5. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.

Needless to say, in the event of the petitioner filing an application seeking discharge, if charges are not framed, the concerned Court shall dispose of the same after hearing both sides, within a period of four (04) weeks.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
